title: Suggi — the harvest tale
subtitle: a folk reading
intent: As in the harvest fables, the patient farmer who counts the grain and waits for the fours to ripen gathers the fullest granary.

start.text: At Suggi, the harvest festival, two neighbours count their grain into the pits. The fable's moral: the one who counts patiently, not the one who grabs, fills the larger granary.
Grain by grain, hole by hole. In the old tales the hasty farmer scatters and loses; the counting one gathers the fours and prospers.

capture.text: A hole ripens to four sheaves and is carried to your granary. Patience, in the harvest fables, is always rewarded in fours.
Four gathered. The wise farmer sows the big handful where it will ripen the most holes, not merely the nearest.
Into the granary. The tale repeats: count, wait, and the harvest falls to the patient.

win.text: The fields are bare and your granary is fullest. The fable ends as it always does — the careful counter prospers.

lose.text: The neighbour's granary is fuller this year. Even a fable forgives one poor harvest; count more patiently next time.
